Antipas's domains, Galilee and Perea, after his exile in 39
'the former territories of Herod Archelaus' (Judea, Samaria and Idumea), given by Claudius in 41

successors.note: The Herod Agrippa page: Claudius made Judea a Roman province under the procurator Cuspius Fadus (tenure 44-46). Galilee, Perea and the north after 44 are not on the page.

capitals.name: Jerusalem
capitals.note: The page names no official capital: it calls Jerusalem 'his religious capital' and Caesarea his 'little Rome'. No seat is given for 37-40.

rulers.title: king
rulers.note: Infobox: Iturea and the north AD 37-44, Galilee and Perea AD 40-44 (the article also has 39), Judea, Samaria and Idumea AD 41-44.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). The page says Abila was given in 41, not 37, but names Lysanias's tetrarchy in 37; the Abila circle is a reading. No area on the page.

correction.text: adds Antipas's Galilee and Perea (the page: 39 in the text, 40 in the infobox)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Galilee and Gilead (Peraea) added.

correction.text: adds the former territories of Herod Archelaus; his realm 'as vast as that of his grandfather Herod the Great'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Judea, Samaria and Idumea added with the judea dossier's own spec for Archelaus's ethnarchy. 'As vast as' Herod the Great's, whose Cliopatria Judea shape is 31,900 km2: the realm here is the union of the four parts, with the Hauran counted once.

region.text: the tetrarchies of Philip and Lysanias

ledger.note: 37: Caligula makes Agrippa king of the north. 'in 37 by obtaining the old tetrarchies of Philip and Lysanias', 'in addition to the title of king and the diadem'; infobox 'AD 37-44'.

region.text: Philip's tetrarchy: Gaulanitis, Trachonitis, Batanaea, Auranitis, Paneas/Iturea

ledger.note: 37: Philip's former territories pass to Agrippa. 'In 37 CE, Philip's former territories were given to Agrippa I, who was made king' (Herodian tetrarchy); added to Syria after Philip's death in 34.

region.text: the tetrarchy of Lysanias round Abila in the Anti-Lebanon

ledger.note: 37: Lysanias's tetrarchy. The page names it among the 'old tetrarchies of Philip and Lysanias' and gives the city of Abila in Anti-Lebanon at 41; the region here is a 30 km circle round Abila.
37: Agrippa is a Roman client king, made so by Caligula (page: Caligula 'granted him the title of king').

39: Antipas's domains pass to Agrippa. Herodian tetrarchy page: 'After the banishment of Herod Antipas in 39 CE Herod Agrippa I became also ruler of Galilee and Perea'. The Herod Agrippa page has 'In 39, Antipas resolved to meet Caligula' but dates the grant of 'Galilee and Perea in 40' (text and infobox).

region.text: Judea, Samaria and Idumea, the former ethnarchy of Archelaus

ledger.note: 41: Claudius adds Judea, Samaria and Idumea. He 'was endowed with the former territories of Herod Archelaus', making the realm 'as vast as that of his grandfather Herod the Great'.
44: Agrippa dies at Caesarea and the client kingdom ends. 'Agrippa I died unexpectedly in 44, after only three years of reign over Judaea.'
44: Judea becomes a province under the procurator Cuspius Fadus. The page does not follow Galilee, Perea and the north after 44; the whole realm is counted lost to Rome.
44: the kingdom ends with the king's death. Claudius made Judea a Roman province under the procurator Cuspius Fadus (tenure 44-46).

certainty.note: No page gives boundaries; the districts of Philip and Antipas are stand-ins (Golan, Hauran, Galilee, Gilead).

sources.title: Herod Agrippa

sources.title: Herodian tetrarchy

notes: Two pages (budget 2-5). Agrippa I's kingdom of 7 years is below the ten-year bar but is the successor of both tetrarchies written in this batch. Disagreements on the Herod Agrippa page: Antipas's lands in 39 (text) against 40 (infobox); Abila in 37 (implied by 'the old tetrarchies of Philip and Lysanias') against 41 (stated). The Lysanias tetrarchy (Abilene) has no dossier and no gazetteer name; Abila's coordinates are the usual site and not from the pages. After 44 the page tells only of Judea; Agrippa II (Chalcis 48, then Philip's lands 53) is not covered and needs a dossier from a Rome-and-neighbours group. Judea's province under Fadus is roman-empire's (eu-04).
